additional_requirements: The binge eating occurs, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

S051.name: Rapid_Eating
S051.description: Eating much more rapidly than normal.
examples: Swallowing food without chewing it properly.
Eating continuously and rapidly to the point where it is difficult to breathe.
Eating so urgently that there is no time to taste the food.
Eating at a speed that surprises others.

S053.name: Eating_Without_Hunger
S053.description: Eating large amounts of food when not feeling physically hungry.
examples: Starting to eat a large amount of food again immediately after finishing a meal.
A binge eating episode starting when not hungry at all.
Continuing to eat large amounts despite being full.
Seeking out food even when there are absolutely no physical hunger signals.

S055.name: Negative_Affect_After_Binge
S055.description: Feeling disgusted with oneself, depressed, or very guilty afterward.
examples: Feeling unbearable disgust and self-loathing after binging.
Falling into extreme depression and self-criticism immediately after binging.
Feeling intense guilt and regret over the fact that I binged again.
Feeling shame that I am pathetic and have weak willpower after binging.

patient_info.stressor_event: Foreclosure on a mortgage or loan
patient_info.stressor: After George and his wife fell behind on payments during a long gap between paid event contracts, the foreclosure process on their home became the first crisis he could not organize his way out of, and he withdrew from some of the community planning roles that usually structured his week. Across the following 1 year and 2 months, evenings that once revolved around cooking for others shifted into repeated episodes of eating very large amounts of soul food, takeout, and leftover event food rapidly and without hunger, with a sense of losing control once he was alone in the kitchen. The aftermath became increasingly painful for him, marked by shame, guilt, and disgust that conflicted with his public image as energetic, generous, and disciplined. He entered psychiatric care after first speaking with his primary care doctor about the pattern during a routine visit and accepting a referral rather than framing it only as stress over the foreclosure.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: What brings me in is that most nights when my wife goes to bed, I end up in the kitchen eating way past a normal plate—like fried chicken, mac and cheese, sweet potatoes, rolls, and whatever event leftovers are there until a whole tray or half the fridge is gone.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: Once I take that first bite, it feels like the decision has already been made for me, and even while I’m telling myself, 'George, stop now,' my hands keep fixing another plate or opening another container.

S051.name: Rapid_Eating
S051.description: Eating much more rapidly than normal.
S051.manifestation: I eat so fast during those times that I barely taste food I used to take pride in cooking, and sometimes I’m standing at the counter swallowing big bites before I’ve even finished chewing the last one.

S053.name: Eating_Without_Hunger
S053.description: Eating large amounts of food when not feeling physically hungry.
S053.manifestation: A lot of the time I’m not hungry at all—I may have just eaten dinner with my wife—but later I still go back and start picking at leftovers until it turns into another full-on spread.

S055.name: Negative_Affect_After_Binge
S055.description: Feeling disgusted with oneself, depressed, or very guilty afterward.
S055.manifestation: Afterward I feel sick with myself, like I’m this man everybody sees as organized and strong, but I’m sitting there ashamed, guilty, and disgusted that I let it happen again.

additional_requirement_1.name: Additional Requirement 1
additional_requirement_1.description: The binge eating occurs, on average, at least once a week for 3 months
additional_requirement_1.manifestation: For months now, I can’t think of a single week where it didn’t happen at least once, and most weeks it’s been several nights after my wife goes to bed.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: I’ve pulled back from community planning meetings and helping with events because I feel embarrassed, drained, and afraid people will notice I’m not holding things together the way I used to.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been going on since the foreclosure process started, about a year and two months now.
